articles.contents:
Profile
Data analyst with a background in quantitative social research (M.A. Sociology, grade 1.3) and experience in the data-driven steering of public infrastructure projects and funding programmes. I design steering dashboards, KPIs and data models and run statistical analyses (regression, panel data) with Python, R and SQL. My analyses fed into the Schnellladebericht and the evaluation of the Schnellladegesetz. I present results to management, ministry and external partners, and work with clean, tested code (Git, pytest).
Experience
Data Analyst · NOW GmbH, Berlin · 09/2025 – present
Built an automated, self-updating SQL pipeline on AWS (Redshift, Athena), replacing the manual dashboard update of charging infrastructure data
Developed a KPI dashboard in Power BI on the rollout status of infrastructure projects across Germany
Prepared Redshift views for self-service analyses, so colleagues can calculate utilisation on their own
Prepared analyses for management as a basis for negotiations, incl. recommendations on bundling sites for funding applications
Automated recurring reporting and mailing workflows with Python and GitHub Actions
Junior Research Analyst · FGS Global, Berlin · 09/2023 – 02/2025
Responsible for a cross-country panel study on corporate reputation (260,000 respondents, 150 companies, 17 countries), incl. harmonised KPI definitions
Developed campaign-measurement dashboards (Looker, BigQuery, Funnel.io, GitHub) and modelled heterogeneous data sources
Statistical analyses and study designs (multivariate/hierarchical regression, t-tests) in Python, R, SQL and Looker
Presented results to business units, clients and leadership; ran workshops and trainings
Used ML models (Random Forest, multiple imputation) to predict missing data
Working Student Data Analyst · KPMG Germany, Berlin · 05/2022 – 04/2023
Quantitative customer-satisfaction reports for management boards; process automation with R
Statistical analysis of research data; conducted and reported international online surveys
Education
Data Science full-time programme · DataScientest, Berlin · 05/2025 – 08/2025
Certified by Université Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne (“Data Scientist”). Project: plant recognition app with a pre-trained CNN (see Projects).
M.A. European Societies (Sociology) · Freie Universität Berlin · 04/2020 – 02/2023
Grade 1.3; thesis “Social and Institutional Trust during COVID-19” (1.0).
B.A. Sociology & History · Universität Trier · 10/2015 – 02/2019
Thesis “Attitudes towards refugees in Germany” (1.0).
Skills
BI & Reporting: Power BI, Looker, LookML, dashboards, KPI systems, data modelling, storytelling with data
Databases & Cloud: SQL, AWS (Redshift, Athena), GCP (BigQuery), Git/GitHub, GitHub Actions
Analysis & Programming: Python (Pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn), R (RShiny, RMarkdown), statistics, survey design, longitudinal data, pytest
Machine Learning: scikit-learn, TensorFlow, PyTorch, Keras, MLflow
Languages: German (native), English (C2), Spanish (A2), Russian (A1), Latin

articles.title: Projects
articles.description: A selection of data science projects – from dashboards and data pipelines to machine learning.
articles.contents:
Charging Infrastructure in Germany

PythonPandasGeoPandasStreamlitPlotlyGitHub Actions

Question: How well is Germany covered with public EV charging points, and how does supply relate to the number of electric vehicles – district by district?
What I did
Built a pipeline that downloads the public charging station register of the Federal Network Agency (BNetzA), reshapes it to one row per charging point and assigns each point to its district via a spatial join with BKG boundaries.
Related the charging points to EV stock figures from the Federal Motor Transport Authority (KBA).
Built an interactive dashboard with a district-level map and filters (e.g. state, charging type).
Automated the monthly data refresh with GitHub Actions. Next step: moving the data to object storage with DuckDB on top, documented in an architecture decision record.
Result: A live, self-updating dashboard. Started as a take-home task for a data analyst position at NOW GmbH and has been extended since.

Live app
Code on GitHub

Plant Disease Recognition

PythonTensorFlow / KerasTransfer LearningGrad-CAMSHAPStreamlit

Question: Can a model reliably tell 38 classes of healthy and diseased plant leaves apart from a single photo?
What I did
Trained a CNN with transfer learning (MobileNetV2) on the Kaggle New Plant Diseases dataset – first with frozen weights, then fine-tuning the top layers.
Evaluated with loss curves and confusion matrices.
Checked why the model decides as it does with Grad-CAM and SHAP, to confirm it looks at leaf texture and veins rather than background artefacts.
Packaged everything as a Streamlit app.
Result: A model that generalises well across all 38 classes, plus a deployed app to try it out. Capstone project of my data science bootcamp.

Live app
Code on GitHub
Reports & methodology

Credit Risk Modelling

Pythonscikit-learnRandom ForestFeature Engineering

Question: Which loans are likely to be charged off, so that lending and investment decisions can be made with risk in mind?
What I did
Worked with the LendingClub loan data (2007–2018): over 2.2 million loans with 151 features.
Reduced it to ~418k completed loans (Fully Paid vs. Charged Off), removed identifiers and leakage-prone date fields, and dropped columns with many missing values.
Engineered features (term, employment length, one-hot encoding, scaling).
Trained a class-balanced Random Forest on a stratified 70/30 split and evaluated precision, recall and ROC AUC per class.
Result: A reproducible end-to-end baseline (notebooks, scripts, saved model) that flags risky loans well and can be extended with gradient boosting.

articles.title: Research
articles.description: Academic work from my studies in sociology.
articles.contents:
Social and Institutional Trust during COVID-19

M.A. ThesisFreie Universität BerlinGrade 1.0RPanel dataRegression

Questions
Did the COVID-19 pandemic reduce citizens’ trust in Germany?
How do common drivers of trust (e.g. income, financial satisfaction, fear of job loss, employment) work in times of crisis?
Do crisis-related institutions differ in how much trust they receive?
Data & methods: Panel data of the GESIS Panel, 2018–2021 (three to four waves, with at least one pre-pandemic measurement), analysed in R. I distinguish social trust from institutional trust in parliament and media, and additionally compare government, political parties and politicians.
Key findings
Social trust stayed stable – there is no corona effect.
Institutional trust in parliament and media increased (a rally effect). Institutions differ in whether it fades or remains in 2021; the same holds for government, parties and politicians.
Financial satisfaction is the main driver of trust in the period and models studied.
